name: Recruit and hire field staff
summary: Field recruiting fills pump operator, equipment operator, bulk driver and supervisor positions for the fracturing, cementing and coiled tubing crews, replacing people who leave and staffing crews that are being added or reactivated. An operations manager raises a requisition, recruiters post the job and run hiring events, screen applicants for Class 1 licences, safety tickets and oilfield experience, and arrange interviews with operations managers who are often in the field. Successful candidates get reference and driver's abstract checks, an offer at the field pay grid and a pre-employment drug and alcohol test before an HR coordinator sets them up and passes them to onboarding. Competition for experienced Class 1 operators, candidates who take other offers and interviewers who are hard to reach make hiring the step that limits how fast crews can be added.

baseline.org_archetype: A listed Canadian pressure pumper of about 1,350 people, roughly 880 of them field staff on rotation or on call at nine district bases, with a Calgary head office for finance, HR, HSE and engineering.
baseline.notes: Postings on the company careers page and job boards, an applicant tracking module in the HRIS or a stand-alone tool, phone screens, in-person interviews at district bases, third-party drug and alcohol testing and driver's abstracts from the registry. Many requisitions cover several identical positions.

unit_of_work: one hire (one field employee recruited and cleared to start)
trigger: An operations manager raises a requisition for one or more field positions, from crew scheduling or a fleet reactivation, or a strong unsolicited applicant arrives for an evergreen posting.
end_state: The candidate has accepted the offer, passed the pre-employment checks and is set up in the HRIS with a start date and rotation, or the search for this position is stopped.

volume.seasonality: Hiring peaks in August to October ahead of the winter season and in May to July after break-up recalls fall short; it nearly stopped from April 2020 to early 2021 and surged in 2021-2022.

evidence.note: About 880 field staff with 25-35% annual turnover gives 18-26 replacement hires a month, plus growth hires in 2021-2022; agrees with the organisation file's 10-30-60.

surge.cause: Crew reactivation hiring drive when a parked fleet or crew is restarted

evidence.note: Adding field crews was difficult because of challenges attracting and retaining qualified personnel, and the company held recruiting events (src4); the multiplier is the organisation file's tier C estimate.
Eight field recruiters; about half their time goes to field hires at 30 a month (about 9 hours each), the rest to office hires, campus and job fairs, and sourcing pipelines for the next season.
Approves requisitions against the headcount plan and pay exceptions.
Hiring manager for fracturing positions; cementing and coiled tubing operations managers play the same part for their crews (about 2 hours per hire).
Joins interviews and shop tours for operator candidates when on days off or at the base. Role not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Driver's abstracts, references, offer letters, drug and alcohol test bookings and HRIS set-up. Role not listed for this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: HRIS, field time capture and payroll
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Learning management and safety ticket tracking

resources.name: Crew pickup trucks and light vehicles
District operating base (yard, offices, wash bay, fuel)

steps.name: Raise requisition
steps.description: The operations manager fills the requisition form with position, district, rotation, number of openings, start date and reason (replacement, new crew or reactivation) and sends it to HR.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Approve requisition against headcount plan
steps.description: The HR business partner checks the requisition against the approved headcount and budget for the service line and district and approves it or asks the director to confirm.

control.basis: Headcount control: hiring only against approved positions

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Post the job
steps.description: The recruiter writes or reuses the posting with licence, ticket and rotation requirements and pay range, posts it on the careers page and job boards, and shares it with the field through referral bonuses.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Travel to and run a hiring event
steps.description: For reactivations and pre-season hiring two recruiters drive to a district base or town, hold a walk-in hiring event with short on-the-spot screens, and come back with a list of candidates.

evidence.note: Recruiting events to attract qualified personnel (src4); times and share estimated.

steps.name: Wait for applications
steps.description: Applications arrive from job boards, the careers page and referrals; for scarce roles such as Class 1 operators with frac experience it can take weeks to get enough suitable applicants.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Screen applications
steps.description: The recruiter reads résumés in the applicant tracking tool and keeps those with the right licence class, air brake endorsement, valid H2S Alive and first aid, oilfield experience and willingness to work the rotation, about one in five of those received.

error.defect_description: Candidate's licence class or tickets taken at face value

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Phone screen candidates
steps.description: The recruiter calls shortlisted candidates to confirm experience, licence, availability, rotation and pay expectations, and explains the job and the drug and alcohol policy.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Schedule interviews with the hiring manager
steps.description: The recruiter finds a time when the operations manager or a field supervisor on days off can interview at the base, books the room and confirms with the candidates.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Interview candidate
steps.description: The operations manager interviews the candidate at the base with a supervisor, asks about past jobs, equipment and safety behaviour, tours the shop and rates the candidate on the interview guide.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Supervisor assesses practical knowledge
steps.description: A field supervisor sitting in on the interview walks the candidate around a pump or bulk unit and asks practical questions on pre-trip checks, pressure safety and the equipment they claim to have run.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Decide whether to make an offer
steps.description: The manager and recruiter compare ratings for the candidates interviewed and decide who gets an offer, who goes on hold and who is declined.

next.condition: no suitable candidate, back to screening

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check references and driver's abstract
steps.description: The HR coordinator calls two references and orders the candidate's driver's abstract and commercial vehicle record to confirm licence class, endorsements and convictions.

control.basis: Fleet safety programme under the National Safety Code carrier rules: driver abstracts reviewed before a driver is assigned

evidence.note: Abstract and reference checks are common practice for Class 1 driving positions; times estimated.

steps.name: Prepare offer at the pay grid
steps.description: The recruiter places the candidate on the field pay grid by position and experience, adds rotation and living-out terms and drafts the offer letter.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Approve pay exception
steps.description: The HR business partner reviews the requested rate or signing bonus against market information and internal equity and approves or changes it.

control.basis: Compensation policy: rates above the grid need HR approval

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Extend the offer
steps.description: The recruiter phones the candidate with the offer, sends the letter and answers questions about rotation, pay and start date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Candidate decides
steps.description: The candidate weighs the offer against others from competing service companies and accepts, negotiates or declines; in 2021-2022 many good candidates held several offers.

evidence.note: Competition for qualified personnel intensifies as activity increases (src4); acceptance rate estimated.

steps.name: Book pre-employment drug and alcohol test
steps.description: The HR coordinator books the candidate at a collection site near their home for a pre-employment drug and alcohol test, and a fit-for-work assessment where the role needs one.

control.basis: Company alcohol and drug policy for safety-sensitive positions following the Canadian Model for Providing a Safe Workplace, and customer site access rules

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for test results
steps.description: The candidate attends the collection site and the laboratory or medical review officer returns the result; the candidate cannot start until a negative result is received.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check tickets and plan missing training
steps.description: The HR coordinator copies the new hire's licence and safety certificates, checks dates and the industry training record, and lists the tickets the person still needs before going to location.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Set up new hire and hand to onboarding
steps.description: The HR coordinator creates the employee record with position, district, rotation and pay rate, files the signed offer and test result and sends the new hire to onboarding and training with the start date.

error.defect_description: Wrong pay rate or district set up

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Confirm start date and rotation with dispatch
steps.description: The recruiter tells the operations manager and the district dispatcher which crew and rotation the new hire joins and when they finish orientation, and closes the opening in the requisition.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Candidate declines the offer
exceptions.description: The candidate takes another company's offer and the recruiter goes back to the shortlist.

exceptions.name: No suitable applicants
exceptions.description: Phone screens find no one with the right licence and experience and sourcing continues.

exceptions.name: Failed checks
exceptions.description: References, driver's abstract or the drug and alcohol test rule the candidate out.

exceptions.name: Hiring event
exceptions.description: For a reactivation or pre-season push recruiters run walk-in hiring events at district bases.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from requisition to cleared hire
benchmarks.population: Field operator hires at a WCSB pressure pumper, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate; SHRM reports a 39-day median time to fill for nonexecutive positions in its 2025 US survey (src11), a later and cross-industry population.

benchmarks.unit: hours of mandatory training for a new Class 1 licence in Alberta (MELT)

evidence.note: Explains why the pool of licensed operators did not grow quickly.

pain_points.description: Experienced Class 1 operators are scarce and new licences need long, costly entry training, so postings sit for weeks.

evidence.note: Personnel shortage (src4); 113-hour MELT requirement (src10).

pain_points.description: Interviews wait for operations managers and supervisors who are on location or on rotation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Good candidates accept other offers while references and drug tests are pending.

evidence.note: Competition for qualified personnel (src4); the mechanism is the author's estimate.

sources.title: Trican Well Service Ltd. Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Three Tier 4 DGB fleets (126,000 HHP) operating at end 2022; fourth fleet (42,000 HHP) field ready by end Q1 2023 and fifth approved for early 2024; upgrades include 3,000 HHP continuous duty pumps and idle reduction packages; fully electric sand, blending and chemical equipment developed; capital spending $103.6 million in 2022 mainly Tier 4 upgrades; supply chain challenges such as long lead times on key parts; record inflation; difficulty adding field crews and attracting and retaining qualified personnel; recruiting events; CEWS credited against personnel expenses in 2021 ($10.2 million in cost of sales); the company has safety and training programs; MD&A dated February 22, 2023.

sources.title: Alberta's new Class 1 training: More in-cab training hours, Red Seal certification
sources.supports: Alberta's Class 1 Mandatory Entry Level Training (MELT) requires 113 hours of training including 57 hours in-cab; a replacement pathway follows from 2025.

sources.title: 2025 Recruiting Benchmarking
sources.supports: Median time to fill nonexecutive positions of 39 calendar days (US, 2025 survey).

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35).
The fracturing operations manager stands for the hiring managers of all three service lines; cementing and coiled tubing operations managers do the same steps for their crews.
The HR coordinator and field supervisors take part although the process map lists only recruiter, HR business partner and fracturing operations manager.
A hired candidate also sends a training need to hs-training-and-competency, a link the process map lacks (it routes new hires to training only through onboarding).
Requisitions for several identical positions are split into one case per hire; the posting and approval steps are counted once per hire for simplicity, which overstates their effort slightly.
No external party exists in the organisation file for drug testing laboratories; the wait is recorded with role 'external'.
